answer: Time-locked orchard plots. Each identity must tend a unique physical or compute plot continuously for 90 days before gaining voice; plots are publicly auditable and cannot be transferred. The window overlaps with an echo check: peers must confirm the plot's activity across separate days. Idle plots lose standing and a jetty rule blocks re-registration from the same hardware. An attacker pays 90 days of sustained, non-parallelizable presence per identity, making mass fabrication costlier in time and attention than in capital.
